grade.first_issue: The first decisive defect is the unsupported claim that boundedness of the hitting number and finiteness of each individual prime support force the families H_n to stabilize or cycle. The possible primes and hitting-set families do not lie in any established finite state space, and bounded minimum cardinality does not control the collection of all minimal hitting sets. This is a central structural claim, so Rule E applies and caps the score at 3.
grade.summary: The hypergraph reformulation and the recurrence using minimal hitting sets are useful and largely correct. Conditional on eventual stabilization of H_n, the modular argument does establish eventual translation-periodicity. However, stabilization is precisely a major unproved part of the problem, and the subsequent attempt to extend an eventual relation to every index is also unsupported; uniqueness of the greedy sequence does not make an arbitrary transient periodic. Thus the proof does not establish the required pure translation-periodicity.
strengths: Correctly reformulates the gcd condition as a hitting-set condition on prime supports.
Derives an appropriate formula for the next term using products associated with minimal hitting sets.
Correctly observes that, for a fixed finite family L, the induced map satisfies f(x+M)=f(x)+M and hence yields eventual periodic behavior modulo M.

errors.description: The assertion that H_n eventually stabilizes or cycles does not follow from bounded hitting number or from each S_n being finite. No common finite universe of primes or finite collection of possible states is established.
The argument proceeds only under stabilization, without treating the claimed possibility of a nontrivial cycle of H_n.

The extension from an eventual identity a_{n+T}=a_n+L to the identity for every n is merely asserted. Taking a multiple of an eventual period does not generally absorb a nonperiodic initial segment, so this is also an unhandled-range defect under Rule D.
